title: Test results in a real bug-fix run
intro: Already settled by the spec, so not asked: the factory itself reads the test results (module 5), and commands run through the sandboxed command runner (modules 8 and 9). That wiring is missing in the code today and is a task, not a question. Two things the spec does not settle are asked here.

decisions.title: When a bug-fix run's tests report nothing, what should you get?
decisions.ref: The check after the tests in a bug-fix run (the verify stage). Lands in module 8 and docs/tasks.md item 12.
decisions.context: Today: when you open a bug-fix pull request, its summary line "Tests N passed, M failed" comes from the test result files. If the test command ran but wrote no result file (wrong path, a test runner that does not write one), that line is simply missing, and nothing tells you why. Checked on 2026-11-17: the report the factory builds from no result file says 0 tests, 0 failed, and that report passes today's check. After the recommended option: a run whose tests report nothing stops before a pull request opens, and you get a message saying the tests produced no results. Example of what you would see: "Needs you: fix-the-login-bug, verify: the tests ran but reported 0 results (be.junit.xml missing)".

options.name: What you'll see: a run with no test results stops and asks you; it never opens a pull request that claims tests passed
pros: A pull request you get has always run at least one test
The message names the missing result file, so you know where to look
Asks nothing of you up front; you act only when it happens
cons: A repo with no tests at all cannot finish a bug-fix run until you add one or skip the check by hand (factory skip, which also turns off auto-merge for that run)
One more stop for you to answer when a test command is set up wrong

options.name: What you'll see: the run finishes and opens the pull request, with a line in its summary saying no tests were found
pros: Runs never stop for this, so a repo without tests still gets pull requests
cons: You must read each pull request summary to notice; one you skim can merge with nothing tested
If auto-merge is on, a change with no tests run can merge without you seeing it

options.name: What you'll see: no change from today; a run with no test results looks the same as one whose tests passed, except the Tests line is missing
pros: No new stop and no new message
cons: "No tests ran" and "all tests passed" look the same to you
The missing Tests line is the only sign, and it says nothing about why

decisions.why: A pull request should never look tested when no test ran, and a stop is the only option that guarantees you notice.

decisions.title: When should real bug-fix runs start working?
decisions.ref: Order of work in docs/tasks.md: item 12 against module 16 (the last build step).
decisions.context: Today: a real run cannot work as designed. Every run starts with a command step (the rules that pick bug-fix or chore), and the factory hands that command to Claude instead of running it itself; any check that runs a command (such as "make build") stops with "a cmd gate needs module 9's CommandAdapter, which is not built". Both were checked on 2026-11-17 by running the engine; what Claude then does with a command it was handed was not tried. The automated tests do not show this, because they swap in a stand-in runner. After the recommended option: the command wiring is built next, and you can try a first real run on a test repo once it lands.

options.name: What you'll see: the next change makes real runs work end to end; the remaining module 16 items wait
pros: You can try a first real run on a test repo once it lands
The pilot needs this anyway; nothing else gives you a run you can watch
Shows whether the report formats hold up against real tool output sooner
cons: The four open module 16 items (watch command, two kit versions, live-lock tests, PR polling) move later
Touches the engine's core loop, which other finished modules rely on, so it needs the full 18-minute test run before merge

options.name: What you'll see: module 16's open items close first; real runs still stop at the first step until after that
pros: Module 16 is closed out in one piece, in the planned build order
No change to the engine's core loop until then
cons: No real run is possible until both are done, so the pilot waits longer
The PR polling item needs real runs to test properly, so part of module 16 cannot be finished well first

decisions.why: Nothing else lets you see a real run, and the pilot is blocked on it.
